items.reason: Nested backward disks, volume contraction, exact transport, local nodal axis and first-root axis ODE give all equivalences without finite Z.
At a regular equilibrium DW^T grad rho=grad rho gives eigenvalues1,A; at a critical equilibrium curl forces symmetry, trace2ell.

Simple-root regular-singular axis ODE has a nonzero smooth factor times distance^(1-A/lambda), forcing integer m>=2. No-resonance Taylor induction proves flatness at lambda0. First density term checked separately.

gradP=W+rho e2, Pdot=|W|²+rho W2. Backward error is integrable; uniformly continuous |W|² tends to0. Forward-bounded points are nodal, giving the forward limit-set assertion. No finite-Z claim of single-point limits.
Independent exterior angular ODE, positive limiting derivative and explicit radial factor give global smooth scattering diffeomorphism and exact pullback of far-field density.

Finite-Z center-stable manifolds yield at most two incoming trajectories per zero; strict potential and invariant-area argument give a finite tree and the stated criterion. Its finite-Z hypothesis appears removable by the new independent potential-maximum proof38, still under adversarial review.
Odd m forces a sign change of g, hence an escaping point of the opposite density sign. Its interior scattering angle and the nonzero y-axis coefficient force an angular zero.

new_strengthening.statement: Hdyn iff no interior upper far-field zero, with no finite-equilibrium assumption.
